name: Rice Waffles No. 2
description: Historical recipe from The Whitehouse Cookbook (1887). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: Two-thirds of a teaspoonful of salt
ingredients.originalText: Two-thirds of a teaspoonful of salt

ingredients.name: and a half of milk
ingredients.originalText: A cup and a half of milk

instructions.text: Rub through a sieve one pint of boiled rice
Add it to a tablespoonful of dry flour, two-thirds of a teaspoonful of salt, two teaspoonfuls of baking powder
Beat separately the yolks and whites of three eggs
Add to the yolks a cup and a half of milk, work it into the flour, then add an ounce of melted butter
Beat the whites of eggs thoroughly
Heat the waffle-iron and grease it evenly
Pour the batter into the half of the iron over the range until nearly two-thirds full
Cover, allow to cook a moment, then turn and brown slightly on the other side

source.author: F.L. Gillette
source.originalInstructions:
1. Rub through a sieve one pint of boiled rice
2. Add it to a tablespoonful of dry flour, two-thirds of a teaspoonful of salt, two teaspoonfuls of baking powder
3. Beat separately the yolks and whites of three eggs
4. Add to the yolks a cup and a half of milk, work it into the flour, then add an ounce of melted butter
5. Beat the whites of eggs thoroughly
6. Mix the whole together
7. Heat the waffle-iron and grease it evenly
8. Pour the batter into the half of the iron over the range until nearly two-thirds full
9. Cover, allow to cook a moment, then turn and brown slightly on the other side
